# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Mielke_2025_fluorouracil_pbpk"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Mielke_2025_fluorouracil_pbpk"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/ph18050653>
* Supplement (R script for the 5-FU PBPK model, Supplementary Material S1):
  <https://www.mdpi.com/article/10.3390/ph18050653/s1>

Mielke et al. built a whole-body PBPK model for intravenous 5-fluorouracil
(5-FU) to investigate a patient who died after 3052 mg 5-FU was infused over
2 h instead of the planned 4612 mg over 24 h. They then used it to simulate
steady-state concentrations and AUCs for 138 published dosing records, and
concluded that the steady-state concentration predicts toxicity better than
the AUC (life-threatening toxicity above about 6 mg/L).

# Population

The model is a forward simulation, not a fit. Physiology is that of a 73 kg
ICRP Publication 89 reference adult (Table 1). Tissue:blood partition
coefficients come from the Schmitt algorithm. Hepatic Michaelis-Menten
constants are the means of three published popPK analyses (Terret 2000; van
Kuilenburg 2012; Woloch 2012). Elimination is hepatic dihydropyrimidine
dehydrogenase (DPD) metabolism only, and DPD-deficient patients are not
represented. The model was checked against digitised concentration-time data
from Arshad 2020 (650 and 1000 mg/m^2/day continuous infusion) and Finch 1979
(1.0 g IV bolus) in Figure 1. It has no between-subject variability and no
residual error.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Mielke_2025_fluorouracil_pbpk")()$population)
```

# Source trace

The authors deposited the rxode2 script they ran (Supplementary Material S1).
That script reproduces every number in the Results exactly (see the checks
below), so the model encodes the script values. Where Table 1 prints a
different value, both are listed and the difference is described under
Assumptions and deviations.

| Quantity | Value in model | Script S1 | Table 1 / text |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fat volume / flow | 18.2 L / 19.5 L/h | `VF`, `QF` | 18.2 / 19.5 |
| Liver volume / flow | 1.8 L / 99.5 L/h | `VL`, `QL` | 1.8 / 99.5 |
| Brain volume / flow | 1.45 L / 46.8 L/h | `VBr`, `QBr` | 1.45 / 46.8 |
| Kidney volume / flow | 0.31 L / 74.1 L/h | `VK`, `QK` | 0.31 / 74.1 |
| Muscle + skin volume / flow | 32.3 L / 85.8 L/h | `VMS`, `QMS` | muscle 0.40 x bw + skin 0.0371 x bw (= 31.9 L at 73 kg) / 65.8 + 20 |
| Vessel-rich (excl. red marrow) volume / flow | 2.598 L / 44.8 L/h | `VVR = 3.768 - 1.170`, `QVR = 56.5 - 11.7` | 2.6 / 44.8 |
| Red marrow volume / flow | 1.17 L / 11.7 L/h | `VRM`, `QRM` | 1.2 / 11.7 |
| Skeleton volume / flow | 9.33 L / 7.8 L/h | `VSkel`, `QSkel` | **6.9** / 7.8 |
| Cardiac output | 390 L/h (sum of tissue flows) | `QC` = sum | **401.7** |
| Infusate flow | 1 L/h | `Qinf` | not in paper |
| Kp fat, liver, brain, kidney | 0.2, 0.92, 1.35, 0.98 | `PF`, `PL`, `PBr`, `PK` | same |
| Kp muscle/skin | 2 | `PMS` | muscle 2.19, skin 10.04 |
| Kp vessel-rich | 0.92 (set equal to liver) | `PVR` | **0.98** |
| Kp red marrow | 0.9 | `PRM` | **0.92** |
| Kp skeleton | 0.63 | `PSkel` | 0.63 |
| Vmax | 1221.667 mg/h | `mean(c(1390, 1512, 763))` | 1221.7 (Table 1 and text) |
| Km | 11.70667 mg/L | `mean(c(5.57, 4.55, 25))` | 11.7 (Table 1); **11.1** (Section 4.3.1 text) |
| Tissue ODEs | `d/dt(A_T) = Q_T (C_A - C_T / P_T)` | ODE block | Eqs. 2 and 4 |
| Liver ODE | adds `- Vmax C_L / (Km + C_L)` on the tissue concentration | `RAM` | Eq. 3 |
| Venous blood | flow-weighted mean of tissue effluents | `CV` | Figure 6 |
| Arterial blood | `(QC C_V + infusion rate) / (QC + Qinf)` | `CA` | Figure 6 |
| AUC | integral of the arterial concentration | `d/dt(AUC) = CA` | Section 4.3.2 |

# Dosing the model

The script drives an infusion through a state that holds the current infusion
rate: its initial value is the rate and a dose of minus the rate switches it
off. The packaged model keeps that mechanism in the `infusion_rate` state, in
mg/h. An infusion of `dose` mg over `dur` h is two dose records: `amt = dose /
dur` into `infusion_rate` at the start and `amt = -dose / dur` at the end. A
bolus has to be given as a short infusion because the model has no blood
volume.

```{r helpers}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Mielke_2025_fluorouracil_pbpk"))

# One infusion of `dose` mg over `dur` h, observed on `times`.
infusion_events <- function(dose, dur, times) {
  rate <- dose / dur
  rxode2::et(amt = rate, cmt = "infusion_rate", time = 0) |>
    rxode2::et(amt = -rate, cmt = "infusion_rate", time = dur) |>
    rxode2::et(times)
}

solve_infusion <- function(dose, dur, times, label) {
  sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = infusion_events(dose, dur, times))
  as.data.frame(sim) |>
    mutate(treatment = label)
}
```

# The patient: erroneous versus planned infusion (Figure 2)

The patient (49 kg) received 3052 mg over 2 h instead of 4612 mg over 24 h.
The script simulates both on a 0.1 h grid to 30 h with the reference-adult
physiology; body weight does not enter the model.

```{r patient}
grid <- seq(0, 30, by = 0.1)
patient <- bind_rows(
  solve_infusion(3052, 2, grid, "Given: 3052 mg over 2 h"),
  solve_infusion(4612, 24, grid, "Planned: 4612 mg over 24 h")
)

patient_summary <- patient |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    cmax = max(Cc),
    auc_0_24 = auc_arterial[which.min(abs(time - 24))],
    auc_0_30 = max(auc_arterial),
    c_1h = Cc[which.min(abs(time - 1))],
    .groups = "drop"
  )
patient_summary |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = treatment,
    "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax,
    "AUC0-24 (mg*h/L)" = auc_0_24,
    "AUC0-30 (mg*h/L)" = auc_0_30,
    "C at 1 h (mg/L)" = c_1h
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Model output read from the solve (AUC from the integrated `auc_arterial` state).")
```

```{r patient-figure, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 2 of Mielke 2025 (central curves; the published bands are not reproduced)."}
ggplot(patient, aes(time, Cc, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("firebrick", "steelblue")) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Arterial 5-FU concentration (mg/L)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The model gives Cmax 27.7 mg/L and AUC 82.5 mg*h/L for the given regimen, and
Cmax 4.2 mg/L and AUC 99.5 mg*h/L for the planned one. These are the values in
Section 2.2.1. The Figure 2 legend's "AUC as planned 93.1" is the 0-24 h AUC
(93.0 here), and the 99.5 of the text is the AUC to 30 h. The checks below
compare against those printed values. The model is deterministic, so the only
differences are rounding of the published values (to 0.1) and the solver.

```{r patient-checks}
given <- patient_summary[grepl("^Given", patient_summary$treatment), ]
planned <- patient_summary[grepl("^Planned", patient_summary$treatment), ]
stopifnot(
  abs(given$cmax - 27.7) < 0.1,
  abs(given$auc_0_30 - 82.5) < 0.1,
  abs(planned$cmax - 4.2) < 0.1,
  abs(planned$auc_0_30 - 99.5) < 0.1,
  abs(planned$auc_0_24 - 93.1) < 0.1
)
```

## Concentration one hour into the infusion

The Discussion recommends sampling one hour after the start of the infusion,
when about 50% of the steady-state concentration is reached. Cdyn above
1.5 mg/L would then predict Css above 3 mg/L. For the planned 24 h infusion the
model reaches this fraction of its end-of-infusion concentration at 1 h:

```{r cdyn}
frac_1h <- planned$c_1h / planned$cmax
frac_1h
stopifnot(abs(frac_1h - 0.5) < 0.05)
```

# PKNCA validation

NCA on the simulated arterial concentrations of the two patient regimens, over
0-30 h, compared with the Cmax and AUC that Section 2.2.1 reports.

```{r pknca}
conc <- patient |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id = treatment, time, Cc) |>
  mutate(treatment = id)
doses <- tibble::tribble(
  ~id, ~treatment, ~time, ~amt,
  "Given: 3052 mg over 2 h", "Given: 3052 mg over 2 h", 0, 3052,
  "Planned: 4612 mg over 24 h", "Planned: 4612 mg over 24 h", 0, 4612
)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(doses, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 30, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~auclast,
  "Given: 3052 mg over 2 h", 27.7, 82.5,
  "Planned: 4612 mg over 24 h", 4.2, 99.5
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("cmax", "auclast"),
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", auclast = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated (PKNCA) vs. published (Mielke 2025 Section 2.2.1). * differs from the reference by >20%.")
```

No row differs by more than 20%. PKNCA's AUC uses the trapezoidal rule on the
0.1 h grid, so it differs slightly from the integrated `auc_arterial` state
above.

# Model evaluation (Figure 1)

## 1.0 g IV bolus (Figure 1b, Finch 1979)

A bolus needs a short infusion. Figure 1b starts at about 130 mg/L and peaks
near 210 mg/L, and a 0.02 h (72 s) infusion reproduces that. The duration was
chosen by the maintainers by reading the panel; the paper does not state it.

```{r bolus, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 1b of Mielke 2025 (model curve only; the Finch 1979 data are not reproduced)."}
bolus_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 0.02, by = 0.002), seq(0.02, 2, by = 0.01))))
bolus <- solve_infusion(1000, 0.02, bolus_grid, "1.0 g over 0.02 h")
ggplot(bolus, aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "skyblue3", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Arterial 5-FU concentration (mg/L)") +
  theme_bw()
bolus |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(0, 0.0833, 0.5, 1, 2) | Cc == max(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(time, Cc) |>
  dplyr::rename("Time (h)" = time, "Cc (mg/L)" = Cc) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

## Continuous infusion (Figure 1a, Arshad 2020)

Arshad 2020 gave 650 or 1000 mg/m^2/day as a 5-day continuous infusion. The
paper does not say which body-surface area it used to convert these doses for
the simulation. Here the Arshad cohort median of 1.95 m^2 is used.

```{r infusion, fig.cap = "Model at the two Arshad 2020 dose levels (BSA 1.95 m^2), 5-day infusion; compare Figure 1a of Mielke 2025."}
inf_grid <- seq(0, 120, by = 0.5)
bsa <- 1.95
arshad <- bind_rows(
  solve_infusion(650 * bsa * 5, 120, inf_grid, "650 mg/m^2/day"),
  solve_infusion(1000 * bsa * 5, 120, inf_grid, "1000 mg/m^2/day")
)
ggplot(arshad, aes(time, Cc, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Arterial 5-FU concentration (mg/L)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
arshad |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 100) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, Cc) |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose level" = treatment, "Cc at 100 h (mg/L)" = Cc) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

The model's plateaus are about 1.1 and 1.7 mg/L. Figure 1a shows plateaus of
about 0.19 and 0.29 mg/L, read from the panel by the maintainers. Those are the
model's steady states for 650 and 1000 mg spread over 72 h (about 9.0 and
13.9 mg/h):

```{r infusion-72h}
per_72h <- bind_rows(
  solve_infusion(650 * 5 / 3, 120, inf_grid, "650 mg per 72 h"),
  solve_infusion(1000 * 5 / 3, 120, inf_grid, "1000 mg per 72 h")
)
per_72h |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 100) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, Cc) |>
  dplyr::rename("Rate" = treatment, "Cc at 100 h (mg/L)" = Cc) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

The panel therefore did not use body-surface-area-scaled doses, and
the paper does not state the dose-to-rate conversion behind it. At low
concentrations the model's clearance is about 50 L/h: hepatic blood flow
99.5 L/h in series with an intrinsic clearance of Vmax/Km x Kp = 96 L/h. This
is well below the 224-276 L/h that Arshad 2020 estimated and that the paper
uses for its variability bands. The model was built and validated for the high
concentrations that follow short infusions and overdoses, where clearance is
saturated. It over-predicts concentrations from standard-dose continuous
infusions.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Script values over Table 1.** The deposited script reproduces every
  published patient number to the printed precision (Cmax 27.7 and 4.2 mg/L,
  AUC 82.5 and 99.5 mg*h/L, AUC0-24 93.1 mg*h/L), so its values are encoded.
  Table 1 prints a different value for:
  - skeleton volume (6.9 vs 9.33 L);
  - red marrow volume (1.2 vs 1.17 L);
  - cardiac output (401.7 vs 390 L/h, the sum of the script's tissue flows);
  - the vessel-rich and red-marrow Kp (0.98 and 0.92 vs 0.92 and 0.9).

  Table 1 also lists muscle and skin separately (Kp 2.19 and 10.04), while the
  script lumps them into one compartment (32.3 L, 85.8 L/h, Kp 2). The script's
  own comment gives the Schmitt skin value as 1.04, so Table 1's 10.04 looks
  like a typesetting error. The Section 4.3.1 text gives Km = 11.1 mg/L, but
  Table 1 and the script give 11.7 (the mean of 5.57, 4.55 and 25).
- **Discussion Cmax.** The Discussion quotes 4.6 mg/L for the planned schedule.
  Section 2.2.1, Figure 2 and the script give 4.2 mg/L.
- **Infusion input.** The script writes the arterial input as
  `Qinf * iv.dose`, with `iv.dose` holding the infusion rate in mg/h and
  `Qinf = 1 L/h`. The model writes the input directly as the rate (mg/h), which
  is numerically identical at the published 1 L/h. Because only `QC` of the
  `QC + Qinf` arterial outflow reaches the tissues, the structure loses about
  `Qinf x C_A` (about 1 L/h x C_A) of drug. This is part of the published model
  and is kept.
- **Blood.** There is no blood compartment. The arterial concentration responds
  instantly to the infusion, so a true bolus is not defined. Figure 1b was
  reproduced with a 0.02 h infusion chosen from the panel.
- **Variability bands.** Figures 1 and 2 show bands said to reflect the
  224-276 L/h clearance interval of Arshad 2020. The paper does not say how
  that interval was mapped onto the Michaelis-Menten liver, so the bands are not
  reproduced and the model carries no IIV.
- **Figure 1a.** The published curves cannot be reproduced from
  body-surface-area-scaled doses (see above). The caption also assigns light
  blue to 650 mg/m^2 although the light-blue curve is the higher one.
- **Toxicity analyses.** Figures 3-5 (138 Ma et al. dosing records, the
  literature AUC-derived Css and the decision tree) depend on individual
  patient data and are not reproduced. The 3 and 6 mg/L thresholds are
  conclusions of the paper, not model parameters.
- **Body weight.** The reference adult is 73 kg. The patient was 49 kg, but the
  script does not scale physiology, so neither does the model.
- No erratum or correction notice was found on EuropePMC as of 2026-11-04.
